name: website.buyer
description: RIG homepage buyer-decision gate. 45 categories across 8 families: buyer trust, offer clarity, commercial/money, conversion architecture, vertical fit, offering-type fit, design craft, technical integrity. Scores a homepage variant against what a paying prospect actually needs to see. Input is an evidence dossier of observable page facts, never a self-description. Weights are carried inside each question's instructions as "(family X, weight N)" and sum to 111. Known key set only: the loader rejects extras.

trust_five_second.instructions: Within five seconds, can a stranger say what this company does and who it is for? (family A, weight 3)
criteria: Nothing legible above the fold / Only a slogan, no business
Same, and the promise is falsifiable
Instantly: what, for whom, why you, and evidence

trust_evidence_receipts.instructions: Are claims backed by checkable receipts rather than adjectives? (family A, weight 3)
criteria: Zero evidence of any kind / Adjectives only
Multiple artifacts with provenance and dates

trust_operator_visibility.instructions: Is it clear a named, accountable human does this work? (family A, weight 3)
criteria: Anonymous, no person / Company voice only
Named person, face, and role in the promise
Named person commits personally to outcomes
Named person plus direct contact route
Face, name, personal commitment, direct line

trust_local_accountability.instructions: Can a local buyer picture meeting and holding this person accountable? (family A, weight 2)
criteria: No geography at all / Vague region
City plus local proof (address, phone, events)
Named local person plus reachable phone
Local identity is a core positioning element
Hyper-local trust: name, place, phone, track record

trust_operating_company.instructions: Does it read like a company open for business today? (family A, weight 2)
criteria: Looks abandoned/broken / Looks like a mockup
Real routes plus working contact path
Working contact path plus response expectation

trust_claim_hygiene.instructions: Does the page avoid claims it cannot defend? (family A, weight 3)
criteria: Invented clients or numbers / Unverifiable superlatives
Labelled illustrations plus no outcome promise
Every claim sourced or explicitly bounded
Model of honest claiming: bounded, sourced, negative-space stated

offer_problem_recognition.instructions: Does a buyer see their own broken workflow named in their words? (family B, weight 3)
criteria: Named workflow plus failure mode plus consequence
Adds the moment the failure is noticed
Adds who gets blamed when it fails
Buyer could paste their own case into it

offer_deliverable_tangibility.instructions: Can the buyer state what physically lands in their inbox? (family B, weight 3)
criteria: Plus what is required from the buyer
Plus a sample of the deliverable
Buyer could restate the deliverable verbatim unprompted

offer_differentiation.instructions: Is the reason to choose RIG over an AI agency or freelancer stated? (family B, weight 3)
criteria: Differences plus why competitors cannot do it
Differences are testable against a competitor page
Category-defining: "no one else offers this combination"

offer_boundary_honesty.instructions: Are out-of-scope items and non-promises explicit? (family B, weight 3)
criteria: Explicitly names what the page does not promise
Named non-promises plus why they are excluded

offer_route_completeness.instructions: Can a buyer navigate from this page to each of the four offerings? (family B, weight 2)
criteria: Tier names plus prices where published
Tiers, prices, and what each is for
Plus a recommendation of which fits whom
Self-selecting: every buyer knows their entry point

offer_jargon_free.instructions: Is the copy in the buyer's language rather than the vendor's? (family B, weight 2)
criteria: Deep internal jargon / Heavy technical terms
Buyer vocabulary plus their failure phrases
Reads like the buyer wrote it
Mirrors a specific buyer role's speech

money_price_visible.instructions: Is a price or price anchor visible on the page? (family C, weight 3)
criteria: No number anywhere / Number buried off-page
Prices plus what changes the price
Prices plus what is always extra
Buyer can compute their own likely spend

money_price_justified.instructions: Does the price look earned by the described scope? (family C, weight 2)
criteria: Price appears arbitrary / No scope attached
Adds the alternative cost of not doing it
Adds quantified buyer-side cost of the problem
Price reads obviously cheap against named loss

money_entry_ladder.instructions: Is there a zero-risk first step that captures intent? (family C, weight 3)
criteria: No free step / Free step mentioned only
Immediate usefulness plus no signup required
No signup plus clear route to paid
Route to paid is the same page
Free step is the sales pitch: trying it creates the buy

money_ladder_coherence.instructions: Is free kit → review → build → care legible as an ordered path? (family C, weight 2)
criteria: No ordering visible / Offerings listed flat
Order plus when to use each
Plus the answer to "do I need the earlier one"
A first-time buyer can pick their step unaided

money_risk_reversal.instructions: Does the buyer know what happens if it goes wrong? (family C, weight 3)
criteria: Plus "what if you stop" continuity answer
Risk sits visibly with the seller, not the buyer

money_reason_to_act.instructions: Is there an honest reason to act now rather than later? (family C, weight 1)
criteria: No timing signal / Urgency is fake
Honest capacity plus what delay costs
Delay cost plus dependency on acting
Timing argument is the page's core logic

conv_primary_action.instructions: Is the single primary action unmistakable above the fold? (family D, weight 3)
criteria: Labelled with the outcome it produces
Plus the secondary action is clearly subordinate
Action, outcome, and next-step expectation all clear
Impossible to miss; competing actions removed

conv_action_availability.instructions: Is the action reachable at every scroll decision point? (family D, weight 2)
criteria: One action total / Action only at top
Sticky, mobile-safe, and never competes with content
Action present exactly when intent is highest

conv_action_cost_low.instructions: Is what is asked of the buyer small, specific, and honest? (family D, weight 3)
criteria: Asks for a sale / Asks a long form
Short brief plus what happens next
Preparation, timing, and outcome all stated
Lowest possible commitment with highest possible information

conv_objection_resolution.instructions: Are the real hesitations answered near the ask? (family D, weight 3)
criteria: No objections addressed / One generic reassurance
Plus "what does this page not promise"
Answers the buyer's private doubts in their order

conv_lead_capture_path.instructions: Is there a capture route that does not require a sales conversation? (family D, weight 2)
criteria: Multiple capture depths by commitment level
Plus measurement wired to each capture
A capture path matched to every intent level

conv_scan_efficiency.instructions: Can a skimmer extract offer, price, proof and action in 30 seconds? (family D, weight 3)
criteria: Requires full read / Skimmable but incomplete
Anchored, and a skimmer cannot miss a pillar
Faster to skim than to read: designed for it

vert_professional_services.instructions: Would a CPA, law firm, or consultancy partner see their business here? (family E, weight 3)
criteria: No vertical language / One generic B2B phrase
Profession, workflow, and their system stack
Names their tools and handoff partners
Plus a worked scenario in that vertical
This vertical would book from this page alone

vert_healthcare_regulated.instructions: Would a healthcare or med-spa operator see themselves without a compliance scare? (family E, weight 3)
criteria: Nothing healthcare-adjacent / Mentions healthcare as a claim
Posture plus boundary statement (what RIG will not touch)
A regulated buyer feels understood and safe

vert_field_industrial.instructions: Would a construction or manufacturing owner find this relevant? (family E, weight 2)
criteria: Pure software language / One operations word
Plus an example in that setting
A plant or site manager would shortlist from this page

vert_practice_volume.instructions: Would a dental or high-volume front-desk practice see their problem? (family E, weight 2)
criteria: A practice manager recognises their Monday morning

vert_portability.instructions: Does the page work for a vertical it never names? (family E, weight 2)
criteria: Locked to one niche / Locked with jargon
Explicit "does this apply to me" answer
Any serious operator can map it onto their own workflow

typ_free_kit.instructions: Does the failure-test kit read as genuinely useful on its own? (family F, weight 2)
criteria: Itemised plus how to use it
Plus it produces an output the buyer keeps
Output plus it creates a reason to buy
Creates the buy for the right buyer only (honest filter)
The kit alone would justify the visit

typ_fixed_build.instructions: Does the intake build read as a productised, buyable thing? (family F, weight 3)
criteria: Fixed scope plus what is included
Included items plus what is separate
Quoting path plus typical boundary count
A buyer could commission this without a call

typ_paid_review.instructions: Does the paid diagnostic read as worth its fixed fee? (family F, weight 3)
criteria: Deliverable plus who can use it independently
The fee looks like the cheap option

typ_care_retainer.instructions: Does ongoing support read as a clear recurring option? (family F, weight 1)
criteria: Separate plus what triggers needing it
A buyer can plan multi-year cost from this page

design_hierarchy.instructions: Does the eye land first on the revenue-relevant element? (family G, weight 3)
criteria: Eye lands on decoration / No hierarchy
Correct order: problem, then proof, then action
Hierarchy does the selling in the right sequence

design_visual_evidence.instructions: Is there real visual evidence — person, product, place? (family G, weight 3)
criteria: All three, and images carry meaning
Visual evidence alone would persuade a skeptic

design_premium_craft.instructions: Does the execution read bespoke rather than template? (family G, weight 2)
criteria: Off-the-shelf obvious / Template with swapped copy
A buyer infers the same care would reach their work

design_brand_fidelity.instructions: Is RIG's black/ivory/gold identity held consistently? (family G, weight 1)
criteria: Consistent plus type system matches brand
Type and colour and spacing unified
Unified and distinct from the template source
The identity is itself a credibility asset

design_mobile_integrity.instructions: Does the layout survive narrow viewports without locking? (family G, weight 3)
criteria: Scroll is broken / Fixed artboard clips content

design_density_balance.instructions: Is the information complete without becoming a wall of text? (family G, weight 2)
criteria: Almost nothing on the page / Sparse to the point of suspicion
Every density level serves a different reader
Long enough to convince, short enough to finish

tech_seo_ready.instructions: Will search engines and link previews understand this page? (family H, weight 2)
criteria: Fully describable by a crawler and a share preview

tech_accessibility.instructions: Can a keyboard user and a screen reader complete the page? (family H, weight 2)
criteria: Contrast plus reduced-motion and focus order
All of the above plus images described
Audited: keyboard, reader, contrast, motion, text-spacing

tech_performance.instructions: Will this load fast on a phone on bad service? (family H, weight 2)
criteria: Heavy third-party stack / External fonts plus video
Controlled plus LCP independent of animation
All of the above plus no layout shift
Sub-second mobile LCP with nothing third-party

tech_content_integrity.instructions: Is the full agreed content contract actually on the page? (family H, weight 3)
criteria: Present and correctly labelled (illustrative vs real)
Labelled with no clipped or hidden content
Complete, correct, and verifiable against the contract

anti_slop_genericity.instructions: Does this avoid the generic AI-agency look? (family H, weight 3)
criteria: Full AI-slop cliché set / Cliché plus stock phrase
Could not be anyone else's page

authority_posture.instructions: Does the page read as expert-to-expert rather than vendor-to-prospect? (family H, weight 2)
criteria: Standards plus boundaries on who it suits

rules.reason: no usable primary action above the fold
no price anchor on the page
no checkable evidence of any kind

notes.downgrade_2026_09_30: DOWNGRADED, non-enforcing / advisory only -- do not use as a DONE-gate. Evidence: 20/20 ESCALATE on 17 previews + 3 identical-input repeats (09-29 WEB95 lane, decisions 138256-138323 + 138128-138130); which of the 45 questions trips the 0.20 confidence floor rotates between runs; the trust_claim_hygiene BLOCK rule auto-downgrades to ESCALATE as uncalibrated (09-29 plant 138358 detected the indefensible claim but could not block). Calibration attempted 2026-09-30, refused: 0 labelled rows, need >= 30 per signal (530 existing signal labels cover other rubrics). Lift condition: >= 30 labelled decisions per enforcing signal via rig-s1gate label <did> <good|bad> --signal <q>.<attr>, then s1gate calibrate --write.
